answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Each submission hangs on the quartz of a task receipt, and the onyx is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the hollow of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The design leans on session-key rotation bound to work, revoked by a single upheld challenge, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work.
